scope: Actual viewing of every derived contact-sheet file in the four paired common-role Arcanist death windows. Only scratch review receipt created. No additional decode, Engine, Blender, Git, production source or frozen reviewer edits.
image_origin: H264-decoded lossy movie frames assembled into JPEG92 4:4:4 sheets. Full 1200x536 game viewport tiles retained at 1:1 contact pixels with external labels. Every sheet was sent through tools.view_image with original detail; viewing/rendering may still affect displayed scale. These are not saved native Godot PNGs.

ranges.label: first-raider-death

observations: Three foreground bareheaded axe users change from upright to bent knees and backward-leaning torsos, then readable supine silhouettes in the later samples. Weapons remain visible during the fall.
sides.ai_viewed_frame_sampling: Every fourth frame plus range end, exact hero releases/enemy impacts and hero attack/recovery/reset boundaries

observations: The same foreground axe users retain a visually comparable backward fall and supine arrangement at the same labeled frames. No gross new deformation or detached body part is apparent in these game-scale samples.
sides.ai_viewed_frame_sampling: Every fourth frame plus range end, exact hero releases/enemy impacts and hero attack/recovery/reset boundaries

paired_observations: Scene, HUD, hero placement, damage numbers and reinforcement entry visually line up. Raider fall silhouettes are closely comparable; the conspicuous background difference belongs to the changed Hexer presentation.

ranges.label: first-hexer-death

observations: The rear caster near the arch is a dark compact silhouette, partly merged with the arch shadow. Its small size and low contrast make limb/death response detail difficult to resolve.
sides.ai_viewed_frame_sampling: Every fourth frame plus range end, exact hero releases/enemy impacts and hero attack/recovery/reset boundaries

observations: The rear caster reads as a green hooded human carrying a staff with a bright circular head. Its torso lowers through the samples and becomes obscured by the hero/staff area in later frames. This is a clearer human initial response, but the overlapping staffs and dark floor do not support exact hand, ankle or ground-contact judgments.
sides.ai_viewed_frame_sampling: Every fourth frame plus range end, exact hero releases/enemy impacts and hero attack/recovery/reset boundaries

paired_observations: These sheets repeat the same frames 9-39 as first-raider-death; corresponding sheet bytes and hashes are identical within each side. They are one shared simultaneous event window, not independent temporal evidence.

ranges.label: first-bulwark-death

observations: The front-left enemy has a dark bulky armored form and large upright shield; much of its response is hidden by the hero and staff. In the late samples it is largely absent while the adjacent Raider lies down.
sides.ai_viewed_frame_sampling: Every fourth frame plus range end, exact hero releases/enemy impacts and hero attack/recovery/reset boundaries

observations: The front-left enemy has a human armored head/torso and a bright round shield. It bends and drops to the left of the hero with arms/weapon extending; shield and body remain visibly identifiable near the hero at the final frame 786. Hero overlap prevents a confident settled-ground-contact judgment.
sides.ai_viewed_frame_sampling: Every fourth frame plus range end, exact hero releases/enemy impacts and hero attack/recovery/reset boundaries

paired_observations: The same damage markers, adjacent Raider collapse, remaining foes and warning ring align in the paired images. AFTER has a more readable humanoid/shield fall silhouette and remains visible longer within this window; the sequence ends before complete death/settling can be assessed.

ranges.label: first-elite-death

observations: The isolated target is a short horned dark armored silhouette with an upright sword. Later samples show a lowering and sideward collapse with a dark body lying close to the hero.
sides.ai_viewed_frame_sampling: Every fourth frame plus range end, exact hero releases/enemy impacts and hero attack/recovery/reset boundaries

observations: The isolated target reads as a full human in dark clothes with bright shoulder armor and a sword. Its knees bend, torso leans backward, and the later samples show an extended supine body with the sword still visible. The fall has a clearly readable human silhouette.
sides.ai_viewed_frame_sampling: Every fourth frame plus range end, exact hero releases/enemy impacts and hero attack/recovery/reset boundaries

limits: The decoder reports every consecutive frame decoded, but actual AI visual inspection covers only the retained frames on the sheets: every fourth plus semantic boundaries and range end. No claim of every consecutive frame visually viewed. No separate human signoff is claimed.
Death windows cover the short initial response, approximately the first 0.97s of death. This does not certify complete skeletal death, final settling, ground contact or eventual fading.

Dark rear enemies, shared hero/enemy staff silhouettes and hero overlap limit anatomical and ground-contact judgments. JPEG/H264 artifacts and ordinary game-scale actor size prevent precise joint or mesh measurements.
Raider and Hexer label directories repeat one simultaneous event window and identical sheets within each side; they do not add independent temporal samples.
No whole-movie viewing, physical phone performance, source revalidation or release approval is claimed.
conclusion: Matching game-scale event windows support recognizable Raider initial falls and clearer humanoid Hexer, Bulwark and Elite presentations in AFTER. Elite backward collapse is especially readable. No gross new torn/disconnected body geometry is apparent in the viewed samples; full death/settling remains outside these ranges.
reviewer_type: AI visual inspection through tools.view_image; no separate human signoff claimed
